title: Oak of Perun and Aurochs Horn (9th–10th c. pagan finds)
artist: Unknown (9th–10th century; photo by Anatoly Pm)
subject: The sacred oak of Perun and a sacrificial aurochs horn
description: Museum display of 9th–10th century pagan Slavic finds: the 'Oak of Perun' (the sacred tree of the thunder god) and an aurochs horn used in sacrifice. Among the few genuine archaeological objects directly tied to a named pre-Christian Slavic god.
alt: The sacred oak of Perun and a sacrificial aurochs horn — Oak of Perun and Aurochs Horn (9th–10th c. pagan finds)

title: Pagan Idol and Paganism Display, 9th–10th c. (Kyiv History Museum)
artist: Unknown (9th–10th century; photo by Anatoly Pm)
subject: Pagan idol, the oak of Perun, and sacrificial horn
description: A museum display of 9th–10th century Slavic paganism: a pagan idol, the oak of Perun (god of thunder), and an aurochs horn for sacrifice — material culture of the very pantheon whose idols Vladimir of Kiev destroyed in 980 CE.
alt: Pagan idol, the oak of Perun, and sacrificial horn — Pagan Idol and Paganism Display, 9th–10th c. (Kyiv History Museum)

title: The Seven Gods of Slavic Theo-Cosmology
subject: The seven major deities of the reconstructed Slavic pantheon, emanating from Rod
description: A modern artistic rendering of the seven major deities of Slavic theo-cosmology, presented as a hierarchy emanating from Rod (the supreme god of generation). NOTE: a modern reconstruction/interpretation — presented as such, not as a historical source.
alt: The seven major deities of the reconstructed Slavic pantheon, emanating from Rod — The Seven Gods of Slavic Theo-Cosmology

title: Triglav ('Three-Headed') Cosmological Diagram
subject: The three-headed Triglav: Svarog, Perun and Veles as the three worlds of Slavic cosmology
description: A diagram of the cosmology represented by the Slavic god Triglav ('Three-Headed'): his three heads are interpreted as Svarog, Perun and Veles, representing the three worlds of Slavic cosmology (sky, earth, underworld). NOTE: a modern interpretive scheme — the three-headed idol is a folk/late motif, and this mapping is scholarly reconstruction.
alt: The three-headed Triglav: Svarog, Perun and Veles as the three worlds of Slavic cosmology — Triglav ('Three-Headed') Cosmological Diagram

title: The Bogatyrs (Добрыня Никитич, Илья Муромец, Алёша Попович)
subject: The three great bogatyrs (heroes) of Russian folk epic
description: Viktor Vasnetsov's famous 1898 painting of the three great bogatyrs (heroic knights) of the Russian bylinas: Dobrynya Nikitich, Ilya Muromets, and Alyosha Popovich. The bogatyrs stand in the tradition of the semi-divine epic heroes (Il'ya Muromets is counted among the 'sons of Veles' in folk belief). A defining image of 19th-century Slavic mythology revival.
alt: The three great bogatyrs (heroes) of Russian folk epic — The Bogatyrs (Добрыня Никитич, Илья Муромец, Алёша Попович)
